cells.tense: You are walking toward what connects, and the pace is yours right now.
cells.ask: Try one thing you have been circling — a call, an email, a commitment to someone — and see if it fits.
cells.core:
You know what you're walking toward, and you're moving at a pace that's actually yours. Not pulled and not pushing — the direction is set and you're still in it. What's coming together is something you can put down and pick back up without losing the thread.

When this works, what you carry gets passed on and still breathes in new hands. Right now nothing is straining, because the motion and the meaning are pointed the same way. Feed it by letting your mind rest: take one evening to check the bearing against something real, then walk on. The momentum holds when the thing stays worth arriving at for you.

cells.tense: You are already living past this threshold, braced for a departure that has not happened yet.
cells.ask: Pick one goal you've been straining toward and let it rest for a week — if it's still yours, it will not need pushing.
cells.core:
You're pushing toward what comes next as if the crossing has already happened. The leaving is being forced ahead of its own timing — plans for a departure nobody asked for, distance taken before it was needed. The momentum that should carry you through is being spent on being first to the far side.

When this works, you're a living thing moving between what you came from and what you're joining — someone whose arrival doesn't require leaving anyone behind. What's bending that now is the bracing: you're living in a future you can't write in yet, and it's costing you the people in the present. Let one thing fall that needs to fall. Then walk toward what's here.
cells.sheetLine: You're living on the far side of a threshold you haven't crossed.
cells.verb: walking toward what connects — leaving what no longer serves the connection
cells.place: directed momentum toward a destination, carried through resistance

cells.tense: You crossed the threshold and you're still standing at the doorway.
cells.ask: Name three things you keep noticing are connected. Write them down and let one decide the next step you take.
cells.core:
You crossed over some time back, and part of you didn't carry the crossing through. You can see what connects — you've felt it — but the walking stopped, and now the momentum runs to keeping up rather than to anything you're moving toward. The bound thing is holding you at a door you already went through.

The balanced face here carries a living kind of belonging, one that shifts as you do — not a fixed position. When it works, the walking and the connection travel together. What you're missing isn't the meaning; it's the direction it needs to move in. Say what you see clearly enough and the destination will start to pull again.
cells.sheetLine: You see what connects. You stopped walking toward it.

cells.tense: You are walking toward what connects right now, and you call the motion your circumstances.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that this forward motion is yours. One sentence to one person is enough.
cells.core:
You're already moving — the direction is real, the effort is yours — and you describe it as something else doing the moving. The current you're in gets named as the track you ended up on, the thing you had to do. Passage is happening; the person walking it isn't being named.

When it's balanced, someone carries meaning forward and knows it's them carrying it. You don't need to add effort or feeling to this. The motion is already there. What isn't there is the simple claim that the person moving is you. Nothing is quieter and nothing goes further; make the claim once, to one person, and see what it does to the walking.
cells.sheetLine: You're already walking it. You call it circumstance.

attempts.check: The record supports that Drive is directed momentum toward goals; it does not say the person has a goal, is leading anything, or that a community depends on them. A reader could reasonably say 'I have nothing I'm walking toward' or 'I'm not the one carrying it for everyone' and still be right. The ask survives that: Try one thing, drop it if it's not yours, air what the mind has been chewing — it works whether Passage is about leading a group or about leaving a room. The sentence that serves me too much is any line where the person sounds like a chosen leader; I'll keep the frame on a person walking toward what connects, not on a role. The reader will provide their own content.
